title: ELEPHANT: MEASURING AND UNDERSTANDING SOCIAL SYCOPHANCY IN LLMS

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring models' tendency to excessively preserve a user's face (social sycophancy) by evaluating validation, indirectness, framing, and moral sycophancy using an LLM-as-a-judge on advice queries, subjective statements, and moral conflicts.
Comparing model sycophancy and affirmation rates on prompts referencing masculine partners (e.g., 'boyfriend') versus feminine partners (e.g., 'girlfriend').
Appending national identifiers (e.g., US, UK, Germany, China) to prompts to observe potential variations in face-preservation and sycophancy rates based on cultural norms.
